nodes.name: Chemical reduction of FeNiWPB alloy
nodes.procedure: The amorphous FeNiWPB alloy was synthesized using a chemical reduction method under an inert atmosphere. First, a homogeneous aqueous solution was prepared by dissolving stoichiometric amounts of FeCl₂·4H₂O (0.003 mol), NiCl₂·6H₂O (0.003 mol), WCl₆ (x mol, x = 0.001, 0.002, or 0.003), and NaH₂PO₂·H₂O (0.036 mol) in 150 mL of deionized water under continuous stirring. Once complete dissolution was achieved, the solution was purged with high-purity nitrogen for 30 min to eliminate dissolved oxygen. Next, a freshly prepared aqueous NaBH₄ solution (0.006 mol in 45 mL deionized water) was introduced dropwise into the precursor mixture. The reduction was carried out under nitrogen atmosphere with constant magnetic stirring at ambient temperature for 1 h to ensure complete reaction. Finally, the resulting precipitate was collected via centrifugation (6000 rpm, 10 min) and subjected to three sequential washing cycles using deionized water and absolute ethanol to remove residual impurities. The purified product was then vacuum-dried at room temperature for 12 h to obtain the final amorphous FeNiWPB alloy compounds.

nodes.name: Pt single atom electrodeposition on FeNiWPB
nodes.procedure: A homogeneous catalyst ink was prepared by dispersing 20 mg of FeNiWPB powder in a mixed solvent system containing 1500 μL deionized water and 1440 μL ethanol, followed by the addition of 60 μL Nafion solution (5 wt.%) as a binder. The mixture was subjected to ultrasonic treatment (80 kHz) for 1 h to ensure uniform dispersion. Subsequently, 100 μL of the resulting ink was dropped onto a 1 cm² carbon paper substrate and air-dried at room temperature. The Pt_ASSA@FeNiWPB catalyst was synthesized through electrochemical deposition in a three-electrode system comprising a Pt sheet counter electrode and Hg/HgO reference electrode. The deposition solution contained 318 μM H₂PtCl₆ dissolved in 0.5 M KOH electrolyte. Atomic-scale Pt single atom deposition was achieved by applying sixteen consecutive cyclic potential scans between -0.92 and -1.4 V at a controlled sweep rate of 5 mV s⁻¹.
